annotations.title: Unnormalized Newton's Inequality: Full Proof
annotations.content: The complete proof of eₖ² ≥ eₖ₋₁·eₖ₊₁ by induction on n. The inductive step uses the recurrence eₖ(x₁,...,xₙ₊₁) = eₖ(y) + t·eₖ₋₁(y) and shows the discriminant of the resulting quadratic in t is non-negative by the induction hypothesis.

annotations.title: Cross-Product Lemma for Log-Concavity
annotations.content: From adjacent log-concavity aₖ² ≥ aₖ₋₁·aₖ₊₁, derives the cross-product inequality aₖ·aₖ₋₁ ≥ aₖ₋₂·aₖ₊₁. This handles the linear term in the quadratic decomposition of the inductive step.

annotations.title: The Normalization Gap
annotations.content: The unnormalized Newton (eₖ² ≥ eₖ₋₁eₖ₊₁) does NOT imply the normalized version because C(n,k)² ≥ C(n,k-1)·C(n,k+1) means dividing by C(n,k)² makes the left side SMALLER relative to the right. The normalized version requires a direct induction with the normalized recurrence.

annotations.title: Maclaurin Step Derived from Newton
annotations.content: Mₖ ≥ Mₖ₊₁ is proved as a theorem (not axiom) using the power inequality aₖ^(k+1) ≥ aₖ₊₁^k from log-concavity, then converting to rpow. This eliminates the maclaurin_step axiom from the parent proof.
